solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: When damaged, cut down

indicators.note: something damaged is knocked out of shape, so the letters of the first word are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, the four letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A question about when a tree, once damaged, was felled.
explanation.definitionFit: Hewn is the past participle of hew, to chop or fell with an axe, so a hewn tree has been cut down.

clue.text: Philosophy of Orient's left-winger after change of ends

indicators.note: only the first and last letters of the follower's name trade places, the middle staying put

parts.note: a follower of Mao Zedong, the Chinese communist leader, is a left-winger of the East

explanation.surface: A description of an Eastern radical's political philosophy shifting.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearrangement is a precise one: swap the outer letters of MAOIST and TAOISM appears.
explanation.definitionFit: Taoism is the Chinese school of thought founded on the teachings attributed to Laozi, a classic Eastern philosophy.

clue.text: It's behind pupil starting off learning each new subject

indicators.note: the words' starting letters are taken off them and strung together

parts.note: taken as written; their opening letters give the answer

explanation.surface: A teacher's view of a pupil beginning each new topic at school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pupil' is the schoolchild of the surface, but the definition means the opening in the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: In the eye, the crystalline lens sits just behind the pupil and focuses the incoming light.

clue.text: Gave up, and made some hand signals, we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is the spoken form, so the word for hand signals is matched by its sound

parts.note: to wave is to signal with the hand

explanation.surface: Someone surrendered and gestured with their hands to show it.
explanation.definitionFit: To waive a right or claim is to relinquish or forgo it voluntarily.

clue.text: Was happy about a couple of pawns aimlessly moved

parts.note: taken as written
P is the chess notation for a pawn, and a couple gives two of them
to rove is to wander without a fixed destination

explanation.surface: A chess player was pleased with two pawns shuffled about without plan.
explanation.definitionFit: To approve of something is to regard it favourably or sanction it.

clue.text: Part of bridge, say, is being intelligent about opponent

indicators.note: the word for intelligent goes around the word for opponent

parts.note: clever means bright or intelligent
someone anti a cause is opposed to it

explanation.surface: A bridge player who is clever about outwitting the opposition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bridge' suggests the card game, with opponents to match, but the definition is engineering.
explanation.definitionFit: A cantilever is a projecting beam anchored at one end, used as a structural element of many bridges.

clue.text: Guided back to mindful state in East

indicators.note: the word for guided is turned back to front

parts.note: led is the past tense of lead, to guide
aware of something is mindful of it

explanation.surface: Someone guided back to mindfulness, in an Eastern meditative setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'East' here is the US East Coast, not the Orient the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: Delaware is a small US state on the Atlantic seaboard of the eastern United States.

clue.text: Country in which soldiers or workers have broken into song

indicators.note: the people's word is forced inside the song's word

parts.note: an aria is a solo song in an opera
men can mean either the rank and file of an army or the employees of a firm

explanation.surface: A nation where troops or labourers have burst into song.
explanation.definitionFit: Armenia is a nation in the South Caucasus, bordering Turkey and Georgia.

clue.text: Shock about drug — ask for second opinion in case

definitions.text: ask for second opinion in case

indicators.note: the word for shock goes around the drug's letter

parts.note: to appal someone is to shock or horrify them
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Horror at a drug case prompts a request for another doctor's view.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'case' is a legal one: to seek a higher court's review is the 'second opinion'.
explanation.definitionFit: To appeal is to apply to a higher court to have a decision reviewed, a legal second opinion.

clue.text: Working for company, not well

parts.note: in means operating or in action, as a machine is in when engaged
a firm is a business company

explanation.surface: Someone working for a company despite feeling unwell.
explanation.definitionFit: Infirm means physically weak, especially through age or illness.

clue.text: Strictness with truth, following this rule, ultimately

indicators.note: the word for truth comes after those end letters
ultimately points to the final letter of each of the two words

parts.note: taken as written; their final letters are S and E
verity is a formal word for truth

explanation.surface: A demand for strict truth in keeping with a rule.
explanation.definitionFit: Severity is harshness or sternness, the quality of being strict and uncompromising.

clue.text: Unusually deviant animal's a kind of marsupial

indicators.note: arranged in an unusual way, so the letters of the two words are reordered

parts.note: taken as written, fourteen letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An odd, deviant creature turns out to be a pouched mammal.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram fodder is the clue's own description of the beast, so the surface feels almost literal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tasmanian devil is a carnivorous pouched mammal found on the island of Tasmania.

clue.text: Time chart I organised for school subject

indicators.note: organised means set in a new order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, ten letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A teacher draws up a timetable for a school subject.
explanation.definitionFit: Arithmetic, the study of numbers and calculation, is a basic lesson taught in schools.

clue.text: Like many flying from Kenya via Nairobi

indicators.note: the answer is taken from within the run of letters across these words

parts.note: taken as written; the answer runs from the end of Kenya into Nairobi

explanation.surface: Travellers flying out of Kenya by way of its capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flying' suggests air passengers, but the definition means creatures that fly, namely birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Avian means relating to birds, and most birds take to the air.

clue.text: Overlook writings about one of the Romans

indicators.note: the abbreviation for writings goes around the Roman numeral

parts.note: MSS is the abbreviation for manuscripts
I is one in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Neglecting something in texts concerning an ancient Roman.
explanation.definitionFit: To miss something is to fail to notice it, to overlook it.

clue.text: Write up piece of music as, also, dance tune

indicators.note: in a down entry, writing up means placing the letters from bottom to top, so they are reversed

parts.note: a bar is a short measured section of music
taken as written
and adds something, as also does

explanation.surface: A composer writes up a passage of music that also serves as a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A saraband is a slow, stately Spanish dance in triple time, and the music written for it.

clue.text: Sign that's oddly placed in airliners

indicators.note: oddly picks the letters in odd-numbered positions of the word

parts.note: taken as written; its first, third, fifth, seventh and ninth letters give the answer

explanation.surface: A sign strangely positioned inside passenger aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: Aries, the Ram, is the first sign of the zodiac.

clue.text: Fragment from the star that's exploded

indicators.note: something exploded is blown apart, so the letters are scattered and reformed

parts.note: taken as written, seven letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Debris from a supernova, a star that blew up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fragment' reads as a noun, a piece of debris, but it is the verb meaning to break into pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To shatter is to break suddenly into many small pieces.

clue.text: Bird fell rapidly from sky in America? Doesn't sound like it

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the pigeon-like bird, rhyming with love

definitions.text: fell rapidly from sky in America
definitions.meaning: second meaning: in American usage the past tense of dive, rhyming with drove

explanation.walkthrough: The tail remark points out that the two senses are spelt alike but pronounced differently.
explanation.definitionFit: The bird is a dove, and Americans say a plane dove where Britons say it dived.

clue.text: On which gymnasts may perform as sign of equality, perhaps

definitions.meaning: first meaning: gymnastics apparatus, the high bar and parallel bars
second meaning: the equals sign is drawn as two level strokes

explanation.definitionFit: Gymnasts swing on horizontal bars, and the equals sign is a pair of short lines lying flat.

clue.text: What's repeated in jazz variation for their instrument

indicators.note: a variation is a rearranged version, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: the only letter that appears twice in jazz is Z
taken as written

explanation.surface: Jazz musicians repeating a variation for their instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A zither is a stringed instrument with many strings over a flat soundbox, played lying flat.

clue.text: Just as sailor turned up on bank

indicators.note: in a down entry, the reversed sailor sits on top of the next part
in a down entry, turned up means the letters are read from the bottom, reversed

parts.note: AB is an able seaman
to bank on someone is to rely on them

explanation.surface: A sailor appearing on a riverbank.
explanation.definitionFit: Barely means only just, by the narrowest margin.

clue.text: Exactly reproduced section of whatever bat I made

indicators.note: the answer is a section taken out of the run of letters

parts.note: taken as written; the answer starts inside whatever and ends inside made

explanation.surface: An exact copy of whatever cricket bat I made.
explanation.definitionFit: Verbatim means in exactly the same words, reproduced word for word.

clue.text: Bit of barmy theology?

indicators.note: a bit of the phrase, a run of its letters, gives the answer

parts.note: taken as written; the answer straddles the two words

explanation.surface: A cynical aside that a piece of religious teaching is nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and a sceptic's definition, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A myth is a traditional story, and to a sceptic a fragment of crackpot religious belief.

clue.text: Source of danger in hospital covered by doctor or nurse

indicators.note: the hospital letter is covered by, so enclosed in, the verb for doctor or nurse

parts.note: both doctor and nurse as verbs mean to give medical care, to treat

explanation.surface: A hospital danger as seen by medical staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor or nurse' look like nouns, but they are verbs.
explanation.definitionFit: A threat is a person or thing likely to cause harm, a menace.

clue.text: Having retired, producing short book in a limited edition

indicators.note: the short book's letter is put into the other letters

parts.note: taken as written
edition limited, or cut short, gives its abbreviation ED
B is a short form of book

explanation.surface: A retired author producing a limited-edition pamphlet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retired' suggests leaving work, but here it means having gone to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Abed is an old word meaning in bed, which is where someone who has retired for the night is.

clue.text: Chap who's engaged in monetary affairs not using first name

indicators.note: the first of the two name abbreviations is left out of the word

parts.note: finance is the management of money

explanation.surface: A man employed in finance who never uses his first name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Engaged in' looks like working in the field, but 'engaged' belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiancé is a man who is betrothed, promised in marriage.

clue.text: King poorly protected by the queen in exciting play, for example

indicators.note: the king and his illness are kept inside, shielded by the outer letters

parts.note: taken as written
R stands for Regina, Latin for queen
R stands for Rex, Latin for king
poorly in British usage means ill

explanation.surface: An ailing king shielded by his queen in a stage drama.
explanation.definitionFit: A thriller is a suspenseful novel, film or play designed to excite.
